name: SambaNova SN40L RDU
disclaimer: Package, die and HBM footprints drawn to a common scale (1 unit = 4 mm). Die size (~600 mm²) is a secondary-source estimate — SambaNova has not published exact die dimensions or the full PCU/PMU tile-grid dimensions, so the checkerboard, switch mesh and AGCU counts/positions here are symbolic, not an exact floorplan.

components.name: Package substrate
components.desc: Organic package substrate carrying the CoWoS interposer. Breaks out power and host/P2P I/O (PCIe to an x86 host, plus peer-to-peer links to other SN40L sockets).

components.name: CoWoS silicon interposer
components.desc: TSMC 2.5D Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate (CoWoS) interposer. Carries the two Reconfigurable Dataflow Dies (RDDs) and the co-packaged HBM3 stacks on one piece of silicon, with direct die-to-die wiring between the two RDDs.

specs.label: Packaging
specs.value: 2.5D Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate (CoWoS), 2 dies + co-packaged HBM

components.name: RDD 0 (Reconfigurable Dataflow Die)
components.desc: One of two identical Reconfigurable Dataflow Dies. Each die holds half of the chip's 1,040 Pattern Compute Units (PCUs) and Pattern Memory Units (PMUs), arranged in a checkerboard with a mesh of non-blocking switches, plus the AGCUs that bridge the tile fabric to HBM, DDR and the host.

specs.label: Transistors (both dies)
specs.value: 102 billion

specs.label: Process
specs.value: TSMC 5 nm

specs.label: Die size (per die)
specs.value: ~600 mm², sub-reticle (exact figure not officially published)

specs.label: PCUs + PMUs (both dies)
specs.value: 1,040 PCUs and 1,040 PMUs total ("1,040 RDU cores"), ~520 PCU/PMU pairs per die

specs.label: Peak compute
specs.value: 638 TFLOPS BF16 per socket

components.name: RDD 1 (Reconfigurable Dataflow Die)
components.desc: Second RDD, identical to RDD 0. Its tile fabric is not redrawn tile-by-tile here for clarity — see RDD 0's checkerboard for the shared design.

components.name: PCU/PMU checkerboard (mirror)
components.desc: Symbolic stand-in for RDD 1's ~520 PCU/PMU tile pairs and switch mesh, identical in design to RDD 0's checkerboard.

components.name: Die-to-die RDN link
components.desc: SN40L tile components can stream data between the two RDDs directly over the Reconfigurable Dataflow Network (RDN) switch mesh, without round-tripping through off-chip HBM or DDR.

specs.label: Function
specs.value: Direct inter-die streaming for RDN vector/scalar/control traffic, no off-chip round trip

components.name: PMU grid (Pattern Memory Units)
components.desc: Pattern Memory Units: programmer-managed scratchpad SRAM organized as banked arrays, each with its own fragmentable address-generation ALU pipeline. Paired one-to-one with a neighboring PCU to form a tile. Click **Open** to see one PMU's internals.

specs.label: On-chip SRAM (both dies)
specs.value: 520 MB total, distributed across all PMU scratchpads

specs.label: Aggregate on-chip bandwidth
specs.value: "Hundreds of TBps" of on-chip PMU SRAM bandwidth

components.name: PCU grid (Pattern Compute Units)
components.desc: Pattern Compute Units: the chip's only math datapath. Each PCU is reconfigured per graph either as an output-stationary systolic array or as a pipelined SIMD vector core. Click **Open** to see the header/SIMD/tail pipeline inside one PCU.

specs.label: Reconfigurable modes
specs.value: Output-stationary systolic array, or pipelined SIMD vector unit with M lanes

specs.label: Data types
specs.value: BF16, FP32, INT32, INT8 compute; configurable storage data types

components.name: RDN mesh switches
components.desc: Mesh of non-blocking switches sitting at every tile junction, carrying the Reconfigurable Dataflow Network's three physical fabrics: **vector** (data, packet-switched), **scalar** (addresses/metadata, packet-switched), and **control** (flow control, synchronization, graph-orchestration tokens). Routing uses hardware 2-D dimension-order routing with a software override.

specs.label: Fabrics
specs.value: 3 physical networks: vector, scalar, control

specs.label: Routing
specs.value: Hardware 2-D dimension-order routing (DOR) with software override; point-to-point, multicast, and many-to-one

components.name: AGCU column (west)
components.desc: Address Generation and Coalescing Units (AGCUs): the tile fabric's portal to the outside world. Generate memory addresses for HBM/DDR/host accesses, hold a Segment Lookaside Buffer for virtual-to-physical translation, carry peer-to-peer traffic between RDU sockets, and expose a graph-control interface so the RDU can orchestrate a schedule of dataflow graphs without the host CPU in the loop.

specs.label: Functions
specs.value: Memory address generation (DDR/HBM/host), P2P between RDUs, graph control interface, Segment Lookaside Buffer

components.name: AGCU column (east)
components.desc: Mirror AGCU column serving RDD 1's edge of the tile fabric.

components.name: HBM3 stack (west)
components.desc: Co-packaged HBM3, tier 2 of the 3-tier memory system. Models are streamed from DDR into HBM, which acts as the staging/caching tier close to the tile fabric (not the primary operand storage — that's the on-chip PMU SRAM).

specs.label: Capacity (per socket)
specs.value: 64 GiB co-packaged HBM3

specs.label: Bandwidth (per socket)
specs.value: ~2 TB/s peak

specs.label: Stack count/capacity split
specs.value: 4 stacks × 16 GiB (not officially disclosed; a plausible HBM3 configuration for 64 GiB)

components.name: HBM3 stack (east)
components.desc: Second pair of HBM3 stacks, mirroring the west side.

components.name: DDR5 DRAM (off-package)
components.desc: Tier 3 of the 3-tier memory system: up to 1.5 TiB of DDR5 DRAM per socket, reached through the AGCUs over the host/P2P fabric rather than a GPU-style unified memory bus. This is the key differentiator versus HBM-only accelerators — it lets a single socket hold far more model/KV-cache capacity than HBM alone, at the cost of lower bandwidth, with the RDU's compiler orchestrating what gets staged into HBM and SRAM ahead of time.

specs.label: Capacity (per socket)
specs.value: Up to 1.5 TiB DDR DRAM

specs.label: Bandwidth (per socket)
specs.value: Over 200 GB/s peak; DDR→HBM load bandwidth over 1 TB/s

components.name: PMU
components.desc: Zoomed checkerboard: each tile pairs one PMU (memory) with one PCU (compute), bordered on two sides by mesh switches — the layout repeats uniformly across the whole die.

components.name: PCU
components.desc: PCU of the pair, directly adjacent to its PMU so operand reads/writes never leave the tile boundary.

components.name: Switch (S)
components.desc: Non-blocking switch at each tile corner. Every tile's vector/scalar/control traffic hops through its local switch toward a neighboring tile or out to an AGCU — this mesh is what lets a whole fused pipeline be spatially mapped across many tiles.

components.name: Header
components.desc: Decodes the configured instruction for this PCU and feeds the SIMD/systolic body from the Vector-In/Scalar-In FIFOs and counters.

components.name: SIMD/systolic stage
components.desc: The PCU body: multiple pipelined SIMD/systolic compute stages, each followed by a register stage. Configured per-graph as either an **output-stationary systolic array** (weights held in place, activations stream through) or a **pipelined SIMD vector core** with M lanes doing arithmetic, logical and bitwise ops. A cross-lane reduction tree taps across the stages for reductions (e.g. softmax sum).

specs.label: Stages
specs.value: Multiple pipelined SIMD/systolic compute stages + register stages, plus a cross-lane reduction tree

components.name: Tail
components.desc: Transcendental functions (exp, etc.), casting, and stochastic rounding, then drives the Vector-Out/Scalar-Out FIFOs toward the switch mesh.

components.name: Fragmentable scalar ALU / address-gen pipeline
components.desc: Several stages of integer ALUs with complex addressing instructions (bitfield extraction, shift-and-set). Produces up to 4 addresses per cycle for the scratchpad banks, with address-predication support so multiple PMUs can jointly store one large tensor.

specs.label: Throughput
specs.value: Up to 4 addresses generated per cycle

components.name: Scratchpad SRAM bank
components.desc: Programmer-managed scratchpad SRAM, organized as an array of banked SRAM instances supporting concurrent reads and writes. Data-alignment crossbars on the read/write paths enable high-throughput tensor transforms (transpose, dilation, downcast) in flight.

steps.text: 1. The SN40L socket is 2 identical Reconfigurable Dataflow Dies (RDDs) on one CoWoS interposer — 102B transistors total, TSMC 5nm — plus co-packaged HBM3. Unlike a GPU, there's no SM/kernel split: every tile does the same job, compute or memory, as the compiler assigns it.

2. Tier 3, the capacity tier: up to 1.5 TiB of DDR5 per socket sits off-package, reached through the AGCUs. This is the key differentiator vs. HBM-only accelerators — a trillion-parameter model's weights can live here without ever fitting in HBM at once.
3. Tier 2: the compiler streams the next layer's weights from DDR into the 64 GiB of co-packaged HBM3 at over 1 TB/s — HBM acts as a staging buffer, not the primary operand store.

4. AGCUs are the tile fabric's only portal to the outside world: they generate addresses into DDR/HBM/host memory, translate them via a Segment Lookaside Buffer, and can orchestrate a whole schedule of dataflow graphs without the host CPU in the loop.

5. Opening one die: 520 PCU/PMU tile pairs form a checkerboard, bordered by a mesh of non-blocking switches carrying 3 physical fabrics — vector (data), scalar (addresses), and control (sync/orchestration tokens).

6. Tier 1: weights and activations for the fused operator land directly in a PMU's banked scratchpad SRAM (520 MB total, hundreds of TB/s aggregate) — the operand store the PCU actually reads from, not HBM.

7. The PMU's address-generation ALU pipeline produces up to 4 addresses/cycle into its scratchpad banks, with data-alignment crossbars doing transpose/dilation/downcast in flight as data moves out toward the paired PCU.

8. Data crosses the switch mesh into the paired PCU, which is reconfigured per-graph as an output-stationary systolic array or a pipelined SIMD vector core — this is the same tensor-core-equivalent role a GPU's tensor core plays, but wired directly to its own memory tile.

9. Inside the PCU: header → several pipelined SIMD/systolic compute stages (with a cross-lane reduction tree) → tail (transcendentals, casting, stochastic rounding). One operator's whole compute pipeline is spatially mapped across these stages, not re-issued cycle by cycle from an instruction queue.

10. Results flow back across the switch mesh into the next PMU in the fused chain — e.g. softmax's map→reduce→zip stages each land in their own PMU/PCU tile, wired together by the compiler as one dataflow graph instead of 3 separate kernel launches.
11. For operators that span both dies, the RDN extends straight across the die-to-die link — tiles on RDD 0 and RDD 1 stream to each other without ever leaving the chip to touch HBM or DDR.

12. Contrast with a GPU: a GPU compiles each op (matmul, softmax, etc.) to a separate kernel, launched onto SMs that re-read operands from HBM/L2 each time. The RDU's compiler instead spatially maps a whole fused operator pipeline once across many PCU/PMU tiles — data flows PMU→PCU→PMU across the switch mesh with no kernel-launch overhead and no repeated HBM round trips mid-pipeline.

summary.value: 2 identical Reconfigurable Dataflow Dies (RDDs) on one CoWoS interposer
~600 mm² per die (sub-reticle; exact figure not officially published)
1,040 PCUs (Pattern Compute Units) per socket, across 2 dies; plus 1,040 PMUs
INT8 supported; native tensor pipeline is BF16 (638 TFLOPS BF16 per socket)
520 MiB SRAM per socket in the PMUs (≈545 MB)
2.5D CoWoS: 2 RDDs + HBM3 on one silicon interposer; off-package DDR5 as a 3rd memory tier

scale.basis: 1 unit = 4 mm, same basis as other chips in this catalog. Die footprint derived from a ~600 mm² sub-reticle estimate (not an official SambaNova figure); package/interposer/HBM placement is illustrative.
